newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Scholastic in freefall.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Scholastic in freefall.

text.p: Scholastic Corp stock lost almost 50 percent of its market value in vigorous selling ahead of Friday's market open sparked by the publisher's warning of a third quarter loss and a decline in fiscal year earnings.
In busy third market trade, Scholastic bottomed out at 32, falling from 61-1/2, then started higher to remain in the 34-3/4 to 35 range.

After last night's Nasdaq close, the company said that for the third quarter ending February 28, it expects a loss of between $0.70 and $0.80 per share, including a $0.50 per share to cover a $13 million pre-tax charge realted to reserves taken for retail book returns.
Third-quarter profits last year were $0.55 per share.
Scholastic said it also expects earnings per share for the fiscal year ending May 31 to be between $1.45 and $1.60, under the $1.97 posted last year.
Hastening the descent was a downgrade of the stock by Merrill Lynch this morning to near-term reduce from accumulate and to long-term neutral from buy, traders said.
The Merrill analyst dropped his fiscal 1997 earnings estimate to $2.00 per share from $3.25 and the 1998 view to $2.50 per share from $3.85.

Among other stocks busy before the bell were Citrix Systems Inc shares, which rallied to 33 from 29-1/8, Intel slipped to 149-1/2 from 149-7/8, Amgen added 1-1/8 to 62 after Bear Stearns upgraded the stock to buy from attractive and Dell Computer fell one to 71-1/2.
